- Overestimate prices after sentiment spikes (especially >0.80) — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (<0.30) — add 3–5% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Forecast tends to overshoot 3–5 days after a spike — apply a 1–2 day lag correction downward.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating high/low), reduce forecast volatility by smoothing 3–5% downward.
- If forecast is consistently higher than true outcome over 3–5 days, apply a 2–3% downward bias for next period.
- Avoid overreacting to recent high sentiment — if sentiment >0.80 for 2+ consecutive days, cap forecast at 10% below peak.
